sentences.text:
The instant appeal has been filed by the appellant - claimant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1973 against the [2023:RJ-JP:15069] (2 of 8) [CMA-4006/2016] judgment and award dated 18.03.2016 passed by Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jaipur Metropolitan, Jaipur (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal') in MAC Case No.823/2014, whereby the learned Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the appellant - Samundra Singh (hereinafter referred to as the 'claimant') and awarded a compensation of Rs.1,25,300/- in favour of the claimant.
4.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jaipur Metropolitan, Jaipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts relevant for the present purposes are that the claimant (Samundra Singh) submitted a complaint before Police Station Sendara, District Pali stating therein that he was going from Jaipur to Jodhpur by Car No.RJ-14-TA-5116 with moderate speed and on his left hand i.e. the correct side of the road.

At about 8.00 am on 02.10.2014 when he reached near Sendara, a Trailer No.RJ-14-GC-4699 being driven rashly and negligently came from opposite side and by violating the traffic rules collided with the car of the claimant and due to which the claimant sustained grievous injuries.

5. On the said report, an FIR No.251/2014 was lodged at Police Station Sendara, District Pali for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC and after investigation a charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle was filed for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 &
338 of IPC.
6. The claimant submitted a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.38,50,000/- because he had incurred permanent disability.
7. The respondent Nos.1 & 2 of the offending vehicle did not file reply to the claim petition.

The respondent No.3 - Insurance Company filed its reply and stated that at the time of accident the [2023:RJ-JP:15069] (3 of 8) [CMA-4006/2016] driver did not have the driving license and the vehicle was driven without permit and fitness certificate.
The respondent No.3 also averred that the information with regard to accident was not given to it by the Police.
It was prayed that claim petition be dismissed.
8. On the basis of pleadings of the parties, three issues were framed.
The claimant examined himself as witness in support of the claim petition and also submitted relevant documents.
The non-claimant/respondent did not produce any evidence.
9. After evaluating evidence on record the learned Tribunal passed the impugned judgment and award.
Hence, the present appeal.
10. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the learned Tribunal has erred in passing the impugned judgment and award.
The claimant at the time of accident was about 43 years of age and he was driver by profession and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he sustained serious injuries all over the body with a fracture in his patella bone.
He remained in hospitals for a long period and two operations were done and after operation he remained confined to bed also for about one year.
During the prolong treatment more than Rs.3 lacs were spent.

It was also contended that as per the Medical Board he got a permanent disability of 26.99% with restricted movements of Samundra Singh vs Kailash Singh And Others ... on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112746440/
2 knee joints.

entities.text: Samundra Singh vs Kailash Singh And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that the learned Tribunal has not considered all these aspects and awarded a meager amount.

11. Learned counsel also submitted that nothing has been awarded by the learned Tribunal to the claimant for loss of amenities, loss of future income, for future treatment on account [2023:RJ-JP:15069] (4 of 8) [CMA-4006/2016] of reducing working capacity and permanent disability and also under other heads.

12. Learned counsel further contended that the learned Tribunal has erred in awarding interest @
6% per annum.
It is settled law that interest on the compensation amount ought to have been awarded at least @ 12% per annum.

13. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent - Insurance Company has supported the impugned judgment and award and contended that there is no merit in this appeal and the same be dismissed.

14. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
15.

In the cases of motor accidents leading to injuries and disablements the Hon'ble Supreme Court has pronounced a judgment in Anant Son of Sidheswar Dukre versus Pratap son of Zhampannappa Lamzane & Anr.

entities.text: Anant Son of Sidheswar Dukre versus Pratap son of Zhampannappa Lamzane & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: reported in (2018) 9 Supreme Court Cases 450, relevant paras of the above judgment read thus :& "12.

In case of motor accidents leading to injuries and disablements, it is a well settled principle that a person must not only be compensated for his physical injury, but also for the non-pecuniary losses which he has suffered due to the injury.
The claimant is entitled to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, and enjoy those things and amenities which he would have enjoyed, but for the injuries.
13. The purpose of compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act is to fully and adequately restore the aggrieved to the position prior to the accident.

This Court in Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd. explained "just compensation" in the following words:
15.

entities.text: Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It goes without saying that in matters of determination of compensation both the tribunal and the court are statutorily charged with a responsibility [2023:RJ-JP:15069] (5 of 8) [CMA-4006/2016] of fixing a "just compensation".
It is obviously true that determination of a just compensation cannot be equated to a bonanza.
At the same time the concept of "just compensation" obviously suggests application of fair and equitable principles and a reasonable approach on the part of the tribunals and courts.

This reasonableness on the part of the tribunal and court must be on a large peripheral field."
16.

Learned Tribunal in the impugned judgment has observed that no documentary evidence has been produced to prove that the appellant was driver at the time of accident and he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month by it and, therefore, he is not entitled to claim any benefit of loss of income.

In the opinion of this Court, the Samundra Singh vs Kailash Singh And Others ... on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112746440/
3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: learned Tribunal has taken an erroneous view regarding the loss of future income of the appellant.
The appellant in the claim petition submitted that he was a driver by profession and he used to earn Rs.10,000/- per month.

In the opinion of this Court, if the income of the injured, as alleged in the claim petition was not proved by the claimant, then in order to calculate the loss of income, the learned Tribunal should have considered the income of the injured to be equivalent to the daily wages as applicable on the date of incident.
As per the appellant, his profession at the time of accident was driver.

The appellant has also submitted his driving license (Ex.21)
before the learned Tribunal and, therefore, he is treated to be a skilled labour.
It is an admitted position that at the time accident minimum wage was Rs.209 per day for skilled labour, but learned Tribunal has not awarded any amount in this head.
In my considered opinion, income of the appellant should be calculated as per minimum wages.
Similarly, the learned Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards future prospects.
So looking [2023:RJ-JP:15069] (6 of 8) [CMA-4006/2016] to the age of the appellant on the date of accident, the appellant- claimant is entitled to get 25% income towards future prospects.

17. In view of the abovementioned discussions, increment of 25% as to the future prospects, as per the direction given in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 is also to be made.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, total monthly income of the injured comes out to be Rs.6270 (209 X 30) + 25% (Rs.1568/-) future prospects = Rs.7838/- per month for the purpose of calculating the loss of income.
18. It is an admitted fact that the appellant has suffered permanent disability of 26.99% with restricted movement of knee joints.
Therefore, looking to the nature of work of the appellant, loss of future income has to be treated as 27%.
In this case, the age of the appellant is found to be 43 years.
Therefore, as per judgment of Pranay Sethi (supra) the multiplier of 14 is applicable in this case.

The loss of income of the appellant viz-a-viz 27% disability of the claimant comes to Rs.7838 X 27% =
Rs.2116 per month.
19. Now, as discussed above, when applying the multiplier of 14, total amount quantified as the loss of income comes out to be Rs.2116 x 12 x 14 = Rs.3,55,488/-.

20. Learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- under the head of pain and suffering due to the compound fracture in his patella bone but no amount has been awarded under the head of loss of amenities, therefore, looking to the injuries sustained by the appellant, the appellant is granted Rs.27,000/- under the head of [2023:RJ-JP:15069] (7 of 8) [CMA-4006/2016] pain and suffering and Rs.27,000/- under the head of loss of amenities to the appellant.

`
21. The appellant admitted in a hospital at Jaipur from 09.10.2014 to 11.10.2014 and 22.11.2014 to 26.11.2014 and two operations were done there and thus, total for 8 days he remained hospitalized and, therefore, this Court finds it appropriate to grant Rs.4000/- to the appellant.

sentences.text: The appellant has suffered injuries including compound fracture in his patella bone and he certainly confined to bed also for about six months and thus, he is entitled to get loss of income for six months i.e. Rs.2116 X 6 = Rs.12,696/-.
23. The learned Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.97,300/- for treatment expenses, which needs no interference by this Court.

24. So, judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent as under:
1.

Annual Income (as per the age of Rs.2116 x 12 x 14 = the claimant, multiplier of 14).
Rs.3,55,488/-.
2. Pain and suffering Rs.27,000/-
3. Loss of amenities Rs.27,000/-
4.

8 days hospitalization charges Rs.4000/-
5. Loss of income for six months Rs.12,696/-
6.

Total amount of compensation Rs.4,26,184/-
7.

Less amount awarded by the Rs.1,25,300/-
Tribunal 8. Enhanced amount of (Rs.4,26,184-  compensation Rs.1,25,300)=
 Rs.3,00,884/-
25.
In view of the above, the impugned judgment and award dated 18.03.2016 passed by the tribunal is modified to the aforesaid extent.
The claimant-appellant is entitled to get a sum of [2023:RJ-JP:15069] (8 of 8) [CMA-4006/2016] Rs.4,26,184/- as compensation.
Insurance Company is directed to deposit enhanced amount of compensation with the Tribunal within a period of two months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
On deposition of the said amount, the claimant shall be entitled to withdrawn the same.

The enhanced amount shall carry 8%
interest from the date of filing of claim petition till the actual payment is made.
26. The other terms and conditions of the impugned judgment and award shall remain the same.
